members.name: Heroic Bond
members.note: Group version of Heroism; identical AC/HP magnitudes on Legends. Same line - does not stack with Heroism.

members.name: Fortitude
members.note: EXCEPTION: L55 but WEAKER than L52 Heroism on Legends (AC 17-18 / HP 320-360 vs 18-19 / 360-400). Its value is duration: 2h24m vs 1h12m. p99 also lists it below Heroism (+18 AC / +345 HP vs +19 / +400).

replacement.note: Courage -> Center -> Daring -> Bravery -> Valor -> Resolution -> Heroism is strictly increasing in both AC and HP, so each replaces the previous. Two exceptions: Fortitude (55) is a lower-magnitude, double-duration sidegrade to Heroism (52), and Heroic Bond (52) is the group-cast twin of Heroism rather than an upgrade. Aegolism (60) supersedes the whole line for stacking purposes.

conflicts.detail: Verbatim p99: "These spells are cast by Clerics and Paladins to increase hit points and armor class. They do not stack with Skin line spells or Inner Fire." Confirmed structurally on Buff Lines: Courage/Center/Daring/Bravery/Valor/Resolution/Heroism/Fortitude AND Skin Like Wood/Rock/Steel/Diamond/Nature/Natureskin/Protection of the Glades all sit under the single heading "AC (Slot 1)" and in the same column of "HP (Primary)"; buffs under the same heading cannot stack.
Inner Fire (Shaman 1, +3 AC / +20 HP) shares AC Slot 1 and the HP Primary column with the Heroism line.
Protection of the Glades (Druid 60, +24 AC / +470 HP / +6 mana per tick) is the top of the Skin column in AC Slot 1 and HP Primary, so it overwrites / is blocked by Heroism-line buffs.
ONLY via Aegolism: Aegolism is the "Cleric (Combination)" entry that sits above both the Heroism/Skin column and the Symbol column, so it stacks with neither.

stacksWith.detail: Verbatim p99: Heroism-line spells "do stack with Aegis line, Symbol line, Shielding line, and Talisman line spells." On Buff Lines the Symbol line is a separate column of HP (Primary) headed "HP Only and Requires Gem (eg. Peridot)".
Heroism AC is Slot 1; Aegis-line AC is Slot 4. Different slots, they stack.
Shaman Talisman HP sits under the separate heading "HP (Shielding / Talisman)".
Caster Shielding HP is in the same separate "HP (Shielding / Talisman)" group; its AC is Slot 2.

stacking.notes: Slot map for a cleric-buffed character: AC Slot 1 = Heroism/Skin/Inner Fire; AC Slot 2 = Shielding / Yaulp / Armor of Protection; AC Slot 4 = Aegis line, shaman Guardian, enchanter Umbra. HP columns: (a) Heroism+Skin combined column, (b) Symbol column, (c) Shielding/Talisman column. Aegolism occupies AC "Slot 1 & 4" and the HP combination row simultaneously.

members.name: Naltron's Mark
members.note: Group version. EXCEPTION: caps at 446 HP vs Symbol of Naltron's 525 and Symbol of Marzin's 700 - a group convenience buff, not an upgrade.

members.name: Aegolism
members.note: p99 files Aegolism under the Symbol line, but mechanically it is the all-in-one that replaces Heroism + Symbol of Marzin + Aegis at once. Legends' own effect text carries the classic blocker: "Block new spell if slot 3 is effect 'Max Hitpoints' and < 1100" - Symbol spells put Max Hitpoints in slot 3, so Aegolism refuses them.

replacement.note: Transal -> Ryltan -> Pinzarn -> Naltron -> Marzin is strictly increasing. Naltron's Mark (58, group) is weaker than Symbol of Marzin (54, single) - buff the tank with Marzin and the group with Naltron's Mark. Aegolism (60) replaces the whole line.

conflicts.detail: All Symbol spells share the "HP Only and Requires Gem" column of HP (Primary) - only one can be up.

Aegolism blocks any incoming spell whose slot 3 is Max Hitpoints below 1100, which is exactly the Symbol line. p99: Aegolism is "an all-in-one spell, replacing Heroism, Symbol of Marzin and Aegis with a single buff with roughly the same stats and reduced overall mana cost."

stacksWith.detail: Verbatim p99: "Symbol spells increase hit points. They are cast by Clerics and Paladins. They stack with Heroism line, Talisman line and Shielding line spells."
Skin line shares the Heroism column, so the same rule applies: Symbol stacks on top of Skin Like Nature / Natureskin / Protection of the Glades. This is the key to the best classic HP stack.
Shaman Talisman HP is the "HP (Shielding / Talisman)" group - a third, independent HP column.
Symbol is HP-only; Aegis is AC Slot 4. No overlap.

stacking.notes: Symbol spells require a gem reagent (peridot etc.), which is why p99 labels the column "HP Only and Requires Gem".

members.name: Bulwark of Faith
members.note: Same level as Aegis (57) and strictly better AC (37 vs 34) but shorter duration (1h21m vs 2h24m). Both are Velious drop spells.

replacement.note: Holy Armor -> Spirit Armor -> Guard -> Armor of Faith -> Shield of Words -> Aegis is strictly increasing AC. Aegis and Bulwark of Faith are both level 57: Bulwark gives more AC, Aegis lasts longer. Aegolism (60) subsumes the line.

conflicts.detail: All seven sit under the single "AC (Slot 4)" heading on Buff Lines, alongside shaman Guardian/Shroud of the Spirits/Protect/Turtle Skin/Scale Skin/Shifting Shield, enchanter Umbra/Shadow/Shade/Obscure/Cloud/Mist/Haze and magician Phantom Armor/Plate/Chain/Leather. Only one AC Slot 4 buff can be up.
Shaman Guardian (+24) / Shroud of the Spirits (+28) share AC Slot 4 with the Aegis line - Bulwark of Faith (+37) wins.
Umbra (+29) and the Haze->Shadow chain share AC Slot 4.
Aegolism is listed under "AC (Slot 1 & 4)" - it occupies Slot 4 as well, so it blocks the Aegis line.

stacksWith.detail: Verbatim p99: "These spells are cast by Clerics and Paladins to increase armor class. They stack with Heroism line and Skin line spells."
Same verbatim statement - Aegis AC (Slot 4) layers on top of druid Skin AC (Slot 1).
Different statistic entirely.
Caster/self Shielding AC is Slot 2; Yaulp and Armor of Protection are also Slot 2.

stacking.notes: Best classic non-Aegolism AC on a tank = Bulwark of Faith (Slot 4, 37) + Protection of the Glades or Heroism (Slot 1) + a Slot 2 and Slot 3 source.

lines.name: Armor of Protection line (cleric self AC/HP)

members.name: Armor of the Faithful
members.note: Higher level (49) but only +6 AC vs +15; it buys +260 HP. Not present on the p99 Buff Lines tables, so its slot assignment is unverified.

replacement.note: Armor of the Faithful is higher level but trades 9 AC for 35 HP; neither strictly replaces the other on the Legends numbers.

conflicts.detail: Armor of Protection (+15 AC) is listed under "AC (Slot 2)" together with Yaulp IV (+15), Yaulp III (+12), Yaulp II (+8) and Yaulp (+6) and the caster Shielding line. A cleric cannot run Armor of Protection and Yaulp at the same time.
Same AC Slot 2 heading (Minor->Lesser->Shielding->Major->Greater->Arch Shielding, Shield of the Magi), and its HP is listed under "HP (Shielding / Talisman)".
Armor of Protection's +225 HP appears in the "HP (Shielding / Talisman)" group with Talisman of Tnarg/Altuna/Kragg and Focus of Spirit, so it conflicts with shaman Talisman HP.

stacksWith.detail: Different AC slot (2 vs 1); its HP is in the Shielding/Talisman column, not the Heroism column.
AC Slot 2 vs Slot 4.

stacking.notes: p99 Buff Lines lists Armor of Protection's +225 HP in BOTH the Heroism/Skin column of HP (Primary) and in HP (Shielding / Talisman). One of the two is likely a wiki transcription error; the Shielding/Talisman placement matches its AC Slot 2 (Shielding) assignment and is the more plausible one. Flagged as an open question.

members.name: Blessing of Temperance

replacement.note: Blessing of Temperance is the group cast of Temperance with identical values, not an upgrade.

conflicts.detail: Unverified on classic sources. Temperance is a Luclin-era spell (Cleric 60 on live) that Legends has re-tiered to 40/45; on live it is an HP/AC buff in the same family as Aegolism. Its Legends magnitudes (+800 max HP, +160 AC at level 40) are far outside anything in the classic AC slot tables, so no classic slot statement applies.

stacking.notes: DISCREPANCY: Legends gives Temperance at 40 and Blessing of Temperance at 45 with +800 HP / +160 AC. Allakhazam confirms the levels 40 and 45 for the modern spell set, but +160 AC at level 40 dwarfs Aegolism (+54 AC at 60) and every AC entry in the p99 tables. Treat the magnitude as Legends-specific and do not annotate a classic stacking slot for it without server data.

unlinked.info: THE MASTER STACKING RULE. p99 Buff Lines states it plainly: "Buffs under the same heading can't be stacked together. If a buff (except Focus of Spirit) combines multiple lines they will be listed below it in separate columns. The combination buffs won't stack with the buffs underneath, and those buffs will only stack with the other columns." Every conflict below is derived from which heading a spell appears under.

AC SLOT MAP relevant to a cleric-buffed character. Slot 1: Heroism line + druid/ranger Skin line + Protection of the Glades + Natureskin + shaman Inner Fire. Slot 2: caster Shielding line + cleric Yaulp I-IV + cleric Armor of Protection + druid/ranger coat line (Thistlecoat->Thorncoat) + magician Phantom line is actually slot 4. Slot 3: Ranger Call of Earth, enchanter Augmentation/Augment, shaman Frenzy. Slot 4: cleric Aegis line + shaman Guardian/Shroud of the Spirits + enchanter Umbra/Shadow + magician Phantom Armor. Aegolism uniquely occupies Slot 1 AND Slot 4.

HP COLUMN MAP. HP (Primary) has three parts: the combination row (Aegolism, +1100), the "AC and HP" column (Protection of the Glades +470, Heroic Bond +400, Heroism +400, Natureskin +400, Fortitude +345, Resolution +250, Skin Like Nature +250, Armor of Protection +225, Skin Like Diamond +200, Valor +200, Bravery +140, Skin Like Steel +100, Skin Like Rock +100, Center +95, Courage +20, Skin Like Wood +20, Inner Fire +20), and the "HP Only and Requires Gem" column (Symbol of Marzin +700, Symbol of Naltron +525, Naltron's Mark +446, Symbol of Pinzarn +307, Symbol of Ryltan +158, Symbol of Transal +73). A separate heading, HP (Shielding / Talisman), holds Focus of Spirit +405, Talisman of Kragg +380, Shield of the Magi +250, Talisman of Altuna +250, Armor of Protection +225, Arch Shielding +150, Talisman of Tnarg +150 and the lower Shielding spells.

THE BEST CLASSIC HP/AC STACK does NOT include Aegolism. Because Protection of the Glades (Skin/Heroism column) stacks with Symbol of Marzin (Symbol column) and with Bulwark of Faith (AC slot 4), a group with a level 60 druid and a level 57+ cleric gets 470 + 700 = 1170 HP and 24 + 37 = 61 AC plus 6 mana per tick, beating Aegolism's 1100 HP / 54 AC - and Aegolism would block PotG outright. The cleric should skip Aegolism and cast Symbol of Marzin + Bulwark of Faith on top of the druid's PotG.
Verbatim p99: "Aegolism and PotG do not stack with each other and neither will override the other." So a mis-timed Aegolism locks the group out of PotG for its full 2h30m.

Verbatim p99 on Aegolism: "For stacking purposes, this spell is considered an 'all-in-one' spell, replacing Heroism, Symbol of Marzin and Aegis with a single buff with roughly the same stats and reduced overall mana cost." And on its own page: "This buff will prevent PoTG from sticking."

The Legends Aegolism record carries the classic stacking blocker verbatim in its effects: "Stacking: Block new spell if slot 3 is effect 'Max Hitpoints' and < 1100". Symbol spells put Max Hitpoints in slot 3 (Allakhazam shows Symbol of Transal as "3: Increase Max Hitpoints"), which is the mechanism by which Aegolism refuses the Symbol line.

The DRUID SKIN LINE members, from the provided druid file and the p99 AC Slot 1 / HP Primary table: Skin Like Wood (1), Skin Like Rock (14), Skin Like Steel (24), Skin Like Diamond (36/39), Skin Like Nature (46/49), Natureskin (57), Protection of the Glades (60, group). Rangers share the line at higher levels (Skin Like Wood 9, Rock 22, Steel 39, Diamond 54, Nature 59). p99: "Druids and Rangers have access to this line of hit point and armor increasing buffs."

CLERIC vs DRUID AT COMPARABLE LEVELS (both files' own numbers, max-level values). L1 Courage 4 AC / 20 HP == Skin Like Wood 4 AC / 20 HP, tie. L7-16 Center 6 AC / 95 HP vs Skin Like Rock 7 AC / 105 HP - DRUID WINS this band. L17-23 Daring 9 AC / 130 HP vs Skin Like Rock - cleric wins. L22-31 Bravery 10 AC / 140 HP vs Skin Like Steel 10 AC / 100 HP - cleric wins. L32-41 Valor 13 AC / 200 HP vs Skin Like Diamond 13 AC / 200 HP - dead tie at cap, but the cleric gets it 4-7 levels earlier. L42-51 Resolution 16 AC / 250 HP vs Skin Like Nature 16 AC / 250 HP + 2 HP/tick - tie, druid adds regen. L52-59 Heroism 19 AC / 400 HP vs Natureskin 19 AC / 400 HP + 4 HP/tick - tie at cap, druid version arrives 5 levels later but adds regen. L60 Aegolism 54 AC / 1100 HP (single) vs Protection of the Glades 24 AC / 470 HP + 6 mana/tick (GROUP).

RESIST BUFF CEILING: the cleric line stops at +40 (Resist Fire/Cold/Poison/Disease/Magic). Druid Circle of Winter/Summer and shaman Talisman of Jasinth/Shadoo give +45 in the SAME primary slot, so a druid or shaman in group makes the cleric resist buffs redundant rather than additive.

Legends' cleric levels track the MODERN (post-revamp) Allakhazam level assignments, not the p99 classic ones. Examples: Holy Armor 1 (p99 5), Center 7 (p99 9), Daring 17 (p99 19), Bravery 22 (p99 24), Guard 25 (p99 29), Valor 32 (p99 34), Armor of Faith 35 (p99 39), Resolution 42 (p99 44), Shield of Words 45 (p99 49), Yaulp II 16 (p99 19), Yaulp III 41 (p99 44), Healing 10 (p99 14), Greater Healing 20 (p99 24), Superior Healing 30 (p99 34), Symbol of Naltron 41 (p99 44). Every one of these matches Allakhazam exactly. When annotating, use Allakhazam levels as the level authority and p99 only for line membership and stacking.

Spells present on Allakhazam's cleric list at level 60 and below but absent from Legends, beyond those noted per-line: the nine LDoN "Iony's" adventure utility spells (Lesser/normal/Greater Augury, Exorcism and Cleansing at 10/14/23/24/33/34), Epitaph of Life 52, Mark of Retribution 54, Aura of the Zealot 55, Ethereal Light 58, Blessed Armor of the Risen 58, Ethereal Remedy 59, Imbue Valor 59, Deistic Voice 59, Ancient High Priest's Bulwark 60, Ancient Gift of Aegolism 60, Blessing of Aegolism 60, Ethereal Elixir 60, Marzin's Mark 60. All are LDoN-or-later, so their absence is consistent with a classic-through-Velious spell set.

Lines with NO classic counterpart at all (Legends originals): the Echo line (Echo of Health / Echoing Light / Renewing Echo / Celestial Echo / Sacred Echo) and the Blessing of the Page proc-heal line (Page / Squire / Knight / Lord Commander). Neither name set appears on Allakhazam or p99.

openQuestions: p99 Buff Lines lists Armor of Protection's +225 HP under BOTH the Heroism/Skin column of HP (Primary) and under HP (Shielding / Talisman). Which is right decides whether a cleric self-buffing Armor of Protection loses their Heroism-line HP or their shaman Talisman HP. The Shielding/Talisman placement is more consistent with its AC Slot 2 assignment.
Armor of the Faithful (49) is on Allakhazam but on none of the p99 stacking tables, so its AC and HP slot assignments are unknown. Does it conflict with Armor of Protection, or with the Heroism line?

Legends Temperance (40) and Blessing of Temperance (45) give +800 max HP and +160 AC - values with no classic analogue at any level. Which slots do they occupy on Legends, and do they block Aegolism / PotG?
Turning of the Unnatural (37) does 25 HP/tick against Sermon of the Righteous (25) at 69-79 HP/tick. Is the Legends magnitude wrong, or are the two genuinely not one line?

Several detrimental spells quote damage at level bands far below their own spell level (Ward Summoned 17 "6 (L2) to 14 (L18)", Expulse Summoned 27 "113 (L13)", Earthquake 44 "214 (L31)", Upheaval 52 "618 (L48)", Banish Summoned 56 "529 (L43)"). Is that a scraping artefact or the real Legends scaling?
Symbol of Naltron and Naltron's Mark both carry "UNKNOWN CALC 118" in the Legends effects. p99 resolves them to +525 and +446 max HP - should those be backfilled?

Four records look like duplicates: Invisibility versus Undead / Invisibility Versus Undead (both 11), Improved Invisibility to Undead (48) / Improved Invis vs Undead (50), and two identical Imbue Emerald (29). Deduping would take the cleric list from 206 to 203.
Instill (27) and Ward of the Divine (50) have empty or stub effects arrays in the Legends data. Allakhazam gives Instill "2: Root" with a 1.1-1.6 minute duration, matching the Legends 1m36s.

Legends carries Mass Imbue Ivory and Mass Imbue Jade, which exist nowhere in the Allakhazam cleric list, and lacks Mass Imbue Emerald and Mass Imbue Sapphire, which do. Deliberate server change or data error?
The p99 Buff Lines page has no spell-haste section, so the Blessing of Piety / Blessing of Faith line has no classic stacking statement. Does it conflict with any other haste-type buff on Legends?
